title: Penetration Engagement Sprint Plan and Findings Heatmap
body:
Purpose and framing:
This doc is a sprint-based execution plan for an upcoming external penetration test against Redwood’s inference control plane and supporting telemetry paths. The goal is two-fold: (1) run a tightly timeboxed assessment with clear evidence automation and SIEM handoff, and (2) convert findings into a prioritized remediation heatmap that ties back to RBAC v2 changes, audit log schema work, and CI/CD fixes.

Scope (explicit inclusions and exclusions):
- Included: API gateway auth flows, control-plane UI (console) RBAC enforcement (RBAC v2 feature flags), audit log generation and delivery pipeline, SIEM export endpoints, dedicated/deployed model routing metadata.
- Excluded: customer model data stores (sensitive data isolate), private customer VPCs (unless explicitly scoped in a contract), hardware layer/physical datacenter testing.
- Assumption: testers will be provided with test accounts per the account matrix; no social engineering is within scope.

Sprint model and timeline (3 two-week sprints):
- Sprint 0 (Preparation, 1 week): establish evidence automation hooks, snapshot RBAC configs, freeze non-critical infra changes, onboarding session for testing firm. Deliverables: evidence schema v1, sample logs for SIEM parser, RBAC v2 feature flag export. Owner: Meera Patel.
- Sprint 1 (External test execution, 2 weeks): black/gray box attacks focused on auth bypass, privilege escalation, audit log tampering, and SIEM ingestion stress. Daily sync + 48h evidence review cadence. Deliverables: raw evidence bundles, preliminary severity map. Owner: Diego Alvarez.
- Sprint 2 (Triage & remediation sprint, 2 weeks): internal engineering remediation tickets opened, hotfixes released to dedicated staging, verification by SRE/security. Deliverables: patched components, verification runbook, SIEM parsers updated. Owner: Connor Blake.

Roles & contacts: (quick)
- Engagement lead (Redwood): Aisha Martinez (security-emails).
- External testing firm lead: assigned at kickoff.
- Evidence automation engineer: Meera Patel.
- RBAC / Auth SME: Priya Shah.
- SIEM ingestion owner: Diego Alvarez.
- Product liaison (console): Rahul Iyer.

Evidence automation: design and conventions:
- Central principle: every actionable event must be reproducible from the evidence bundle without access to internal consoles. Each bundle includes:
  - request/response captures (http HAR-style) with masks for secrets,
  - raw audit log slices (NDJSON),
  - container/system logs for implicated services (last 1h around event),
  - RBAC config snapshot (exported role-to-permission table),
  - SIEM export records and delivery receipts (if export attempted).
- Standard file layout (zip): /manifest.json, /raw/requests.har, /logs/audit-*.ndjson, /rbac/rbac-export-YYYYMMDD.json, /siem/siem-transport-YYYYMMDD.ndjson, /evidence/notes.md.
- Manifest schema (sample fields): engagement_id, event_timestamps, implicated_resource_ids, log_offsets. Manifest must be human readable and machine-parseable (JSON).

Audit log schema considerations (what testers will look for):
- Required fields per event: timestamp, request_id, user_id (or service_id), action, resource_type, resource_id, result (success|failure), auth_method, client_ip, region, kv_cache_hit (optional), model_variant (if applicable).
- Tamper-resistance metadata: append-only sequence id, HMAC of event batch (for evidence chain-of-custody; keys stored in KMS).
- RBAC context enrichment: every event must include resolved role(s) at time-of-event and a role_hash referencing the exported RBAC snapshot.
- SIEM export formatting: NDJSON with an siem_source field = "redwood-inference-ctlplane" and fields mapped to the SIEM canonical schema (src_ip -> client_ip, user.name -> user_id, ecs.event.action -> action).

RBAC v2 interplay and test focal points:
- Key checks for testers: role inheritance edge cases, permission escalation via API composition (two-step calls granting total privilege), stale role caches not invalidated after role change, and console frontend bypass via direct API calls.
- Feature flags to toggle for testing: RBAC_VERBOSE_AUDIT (adds role context), RBAC_CACHE_TTL (settable to 0 for real-time), RBAC_EXTRA_PRIV_CHECK (strict mode).
- Expected outputs: for every exploit path, trace must include pre-change and post-change RBAC snapshots that allow us to pinpoint a design vs. cache bug.

Findings triage matrix (quick):
- Severity assignment guidance: "Critical" = remote code/data exfiltration, auth bypass to other tenants, SIEM blindspot in core audit path. "High" = privilege escalation affecting non-sensitive but impactful controls. "Medium" = information disclosure, logging gaps. "Low" = UI confusion, documentation gaps.
- Triage owners: initial triage within 24h by security on-duty, follow-up assignment to eng owners within 48h.

Findings heatmap (conceptual; sample entries):
- Axis X = impacted surface (Auth/Console/Telemetry/Export/Infrastructure), Axis Y = severity (Low->Critical).
- Example cells (textual):
  - Auth x Critical: token validation vulnerability allowing malformed JWT acceptance (proof-of-concept attached). Remedy: immediate patch, rotation plan for signing keys, add strict JWT library validation (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/auth/pulls/834). ETA for hotfix: 48h.
  - Telemetry x High: audit pipeline occasionally drops events under load (observed at 12k events/min). Remedy: increase buffer limits, add backpressure signals, and add synthetic flood test in CI. ETA: 5 days.
  - Console x Medium: UI shows roles without context, leading to possible mistaken escalations by admins. Remedy: add role provenance display and link to RBAC snapshot. ETA: 14 days.

Remediation playbook and acceptance criteria:
- For each finding create a triage ticket (JIRA style) with fields: title, severity, repro steps, evidence_bundle_id, rollback_plan, detection_rules updated? (Y/N), RBAC impacted? (Y/N), SIEM mapping updated? (Y/N).
- Hotfix path (Critical): branch -> small PR -> 2 reviewers (security + owning eng) -> deploy to staging -> 24h monitoring -> push to prod.
- Validation: security runs the same exploitation vector from the external tester (replay using evidence requests.har) and confirms fix by reproducing failure or acceptable mitigation.

SIEM export and parsing runbook snippets:
- Expected SIEM transport: batched NDJSON over HTTPS to vendor endpoint with TLS mutual auth; each batch contains sequence_id and HMAC header X-Redwood-HMAC.
- Parser tips: map resource_type -> ecs.service.type, action -> ecs.event.action, timestamp -> @timestamp (ISO8601). Attach role_hash as ecs.tags["rbac_hash"].
- If a delivery failure occurs, evidence automation should surface delivery receipts and retry attempts in /siem/transport-log-*.ndjson.

Communication and disclosure cadence:
- Daily standups during active test execution.
- 24–48 hour provisional findings report to execs for Critical/High items.
- Final report: includes heatmap, raw evidence bundles, verifier steps, mitigation tickets, and a postmortem within 2 weeks of closure.

Post-engagement actions and long-term workstreams:
- RBAC v2 hardening epic: convert transient role cache to event-sourced invalidation (linked: CONFLUENCE-SEC/rbac-v2-epic).
- Audit log schema v2: extend with role provenance and tamper-hash.
- SIEM export automation: add end-to-end tests in CI that validate NDJSON -> SIEM ingestion using a sandbox endpoint.
- Metrics: introduce a telemetry SLO (100% delivery within 30s for critical audit events) with alerting.

Evidence release and retention policy reminders:
- Evidence bundles are classified internal-confidential. External testers receive only the bundle slice they generate. Redwood keeps canonical bundles for 90 days unless longer retention is required by legal.

Open questions & risks to surface to engagement lead:
- Do we permit remote interactive shells on any internal boxes for reproducing kernel-level findings? (Recommendation: no).
- Who approves emergency key rotation if the test reveals signing key compromise? (Default: CISO + CTO).
- Can we provide ephemeral cloud accounts to the testers for more realistic lateral movement scenarios? (Operational overhead; needs approval).

Appendix (quick checklists):
- Pre-kickoff checklist: freeze non-critical infra changes, snapshot RBAC DB, generate KMS ephemeral key for evidence hmac, create test accounts matrix.
- Evidence pack checklist: manifest, HAR, audit.ndjson, rbac-export, siem-transport logs, short reproducer notes.
- Post-fix verification: re-run exploit, check SIEM receipt, verify role resolution, confirm sequence HMAC matches expected format.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally leans pragmatic: focus on reproducible evidence and tight timelines. The sprint model is designed to reduce context switching while giving engineering a clear remediation runway. Expect follow-up artifacts (confluence playbook, JIRA template) once scope is agreed at kickoff.

Contact and next steps:
- Reply in-thread to schedule the prep session. Immediate action item: Meera to produce evidence schema v1 and sample bundle by 2025-09-12.

End of document.
